briefings.title: Eliot Higgins: How Bellingcat Hunts Down the Truth | Podcast | In Good Company
briefings.tldr: Eliot Higgins, founder of Bellingcat, demonstrates how open-source investigation (OSI) uses publicly available data to solve high-profile crimes like the poisoning of Alexei Navalny, while warning that modern digital platforms prioritize engagement over truth, threatening the core pillars of democracy.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Eliot Higgins, founder of Bellingcat, demonstrates how open-source investigation (OSI) uses publicly available data to solve high-profile crimes like the poisoning of Alexei Navalny, while warning that modern digital platforms prioritize engagement over truth, threatening the core pillars of democracy.

## The Evolution of Open-Source Investigation (OSI)
* **Defining OSI:** Bellingcat utilizes publicly available material—social media, satellite imagery (e.g., Planet Labs), marine traffic, and flight data—to investigate war crimes and corruption.
* **Organizational Structure:** The collective consists of 35 core staff members and a community of 200 trained volunteers, supported by a Discord server of 43,000 members.
* **Core Philosophy:** Higgins emphasizes a "research first" discipline. Investigators must never prejudge a situation or fit evidence into a pre-existing opinion.
* **Technological Shifts:** 
    * In 2012, researchers were limited to Google Earth; today, they can task satellites for daily, high-resolution imagery of specific locations.
    * While Twitter and Facebook were the primary sources during the Syrian war, investigators now monitor Telegram for Ukraine-related data and TikTok for criminal activity.

## Landmark Investigations: MH17 and Russian Poisonings
* **MH17 Downing:** Bellingcat used volunteer crowdsourcing to identify the specific Russian missile launcher and its origin point shortly after the 2014 crash.
* **The "Grey Market" of Data:** Higgins notes that in Russia, government data (passports, car registrations, phone records) is frequently for sale. Bellingcat used this to unmask the Skripal poisoners by finding passport numbers issued in sequential order.
* **The Navalny Case:** 
    * **Tracking the FSB:** By purchasing phone records and cell tower data, Bellingcat mapped the movements of FSB agents and chemical weapons scientists minute-by-minute.
    * **The "Underpants" Confession:** Higgins describes how Alexei Navalny, pretending to be a senior official on a spoofed line, tricked an FSB agent into a 60-minute confession regarding the placement of poison in his clothing.
* **Security Consequences:** Higgins’ work has led to significant personal risk, including surveillance by the FSB and a "cynical" conspiracy theory in the US (the "censorship industrial complex") that currently prevents him from traveling to America safely.

## The Crisis of Truth and Democracy
* **Information System Collapse:** Higgins argues we have moved from a top-down, elite-controlled media system to a peer-to-peer system that rewards "engagement" (clicks) over accuracy.
* **The Three Pillars:** Higgins defines the three core functions of a healthy democracy as:
    * **Verification:** How we know what is true.
    * **Deliberation:** How we decide what to do with the truth.
    * **Accountability:** How we hold the powerful responsible.
* **Authoritarian Capture:** In "simulated democracies," these pillars are replaced by loyalty tests where "truth" is determined by whether it supports the "in-group."
* **The Role of Speed:** Truth must be established within a 2-to-3-hour window following a major event. Once a narrative is established, audiences rarely change their minds, even when presented with verifiable facts.

## AI and the Future of Disinformation
* **Permission to Deny Reality:** Higgins believes the primary danger of AI is not just the creation of "fakes," but that it provides a "permission structure" for people to dismiss real evidence as "AI-generated" if it contradicts their worldview.
* **Limited Investigative Utility:** AI has not yet "changed the game" for investigation, though it is useful for "vibe coding" (writing scripts to scrape data) and providing context clues, such as identifying specific flora in geolocations.
* **Funding Instability:** The investigative journalism sector is facing a crisis; Higgins notes that recent US AID funding cuts eliminated 25% to 40% of global funding for media NGOs, particularly impacting the Global South.

> "Just because you feel something should be the truth doesn't mean it actually is the truth... We want to look at the evidence first and draw our conclusions based off that evidence." — Eliot Higgins

> "AI gives people a permission structure to deny reality. So if they see a picture they don't like or a video, they can just say, 'Well, that's AI.' And that’s the end of their engagement with that object." — Eliot Higgins

> "The problem we've got... is that it treats disinformation as a supply-side issue—that if only we get rid of the supply, then all these problems will fix themselves. But really, that's driven when people feel a sense of betrayal or distrust in institutions." — Eliot Higgins

briefings.title: Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh testifies before Senate Banking Committee
briefings.tldr: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh testified before the Senate Banking Committee for his first semiannual monetary policy report, defending the Fed's independence and emphasizing an ongoing capital investment and AI-driven productivity boom while facing sharp questioning over past financial disclosures, institutional culture, and the central bank's dual mandate amid persistent inflation.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh testified before the Senate Banking Committee for his first semiannual monetary policy report, defending the Fed's independence and emphasizing an ongoing capital investment and AI-driven productivity boom while facing sharp questioning over past financial disclosures, institutional culture, and the central bank's dual mandate amid persistent inflation.

## Monetary Policy & Economic Conditions
* **Interest Rate Status:** The Federal funds rate target range remains held at 3.5% to 3.7% following the Federal Open Market Committee's (FOMC) recent meeting.
* **Inflation and Supply Shocks:** Chairman Warsh noted that while monthly fluctuations occur, underlying long-term inflation is determined by monetary policy, describing inflation as "a choice" and acknowledging that recent price increases have also been impacted by supply shocks such as military conflicts affecting oil prices.
* **Economic Activity:** Economic activity is expanding at a solid pace with moderate household consumption, steady manufacturing output, and a lag in the housing sector.
* **Capital Expenditures and AI:** Warsh highlighted an accelerating surge in business investment and capital expenditures—particularly in high-tech spending and AI-related equipment—noting that equipment investment grew roughly 8% for the year in the first quarter, with high-tech spending logging a 25% growth rate.

## Fed Governance & Internal Reform Task Forces
* **Five Independent Task Forces:** Chairman Warsh established five independent task forces focusing on (1) Fed communications, (2) balance sheet policy, (3) existing data usage, (4) productivity and jobs, and (5) the Fed's inflation framework. 
* **Working Group Composition:** The working groups include prominent figures such as former Walmart CEO Doug McMillian, venture capitalist Mark Andre, and academic economists like Chad Jones and Raghuram Rajan, drawing praise from committee leadership for bringing outside expertise and diverse philosophies, though several members raised concerns regarding the representation of working-class and labor perspectives.
* **Balance Sheet Strategy:** Warsh stated that the balance sheet should be as small as practicable for normal operations and that interest rate policy should be the primary driver of monetary policy.

## Banking Regulation & Capital Requirements
* **Basel III Endgame & Tailoring:** Committee members and Chairman Warsh discussed the ongoing re-evaluation of bank capital requirements and tailoring frameworks to ensure a safe, sound, and competitive banking system that does not restrict credit access for small businesses and community banks.
* **Bank Supervision and Oversight:** Multiple senators questioned the culture of bank supervision and raised accountability concerns regarding past bank failures (such as Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank) and compliance with blackout periods.
* **Financial Disclosures & Ethics:** Chairman Warsh defended his compliance with the Office of Government Ethics regarding the liquidation of private investment vehicles prior to taking office, while Democratic members pressed for more granular disclosures regarding the asset sales and ethics oversight of Fed officials.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **AI Investment Trajectory:** Chairman Warsh predicted that "what is now called AI investment will soon just be called investment" — Kevin Warsh.
* **Long-Term Labor Market Impact:** Warsh stated his belief that over the long term, AI will be "a long-term job creator" and will improve American productivity and real wages — Kevin Warsh.
* **Task Force Timeline:** Warsh stated his expectation that FOMC colleagues will receive early briefings on task force reports by September, with final conclusions and decisions expected by the end of the year (December 2026) — Kevin Warsh.
* **Future College Graduate Employment Risk:** Senator Mark Warner predicted that without proper preparation, the economy could see "30% recent college grad unemployment" within three years due to AI disruption — Senator Mark Warner.

## Notable Quotes
* > "Independence is not a slogan. It is a responsibility. And the best way for the Fed to protect its independence is to stay focused on its mission." — Senator Tim Scott
* > "As I've said before and will say today, inflation is a choice. The members of our committee have no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation and we share a resolute commitment to restore price stability." — Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh
* > "The Basel endgame... is not America's endgame. I am happy to work with international regulators to try to find common views, but we're going to do the right thing for the US economy." — Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh

briefings.title: Fireside chat with Governor Barr on artificial intelligence and financial inclusion, July 14, 2026
briefings.tldr: While generative AI offers transformative potential to bridge economic gaps through increased worker productivity and personalized financial tools, Governor Michael Barr emphasizes that these benefits will only materialize through intentional design, robust regulatory guardrails, and a focus on building consumer trust.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** While generative AI offers transformative potential to bridge economic gaps through increased worker productivity and personalized financial tools, Governor Michael Barr emphasizes that these benefits will only materialize through intentional design, robust regulatory guardrails, and a focus on building consumer trust.

## Opportunities for Economic Mobility and Productivity
* **Worker Empowerment:** AI can significantly boost productivity for low-and-moderate-income (LMI) workers, particularly those with lower education levels or language barriers.
    * **Language Bridging:** AI can act as a bridge for workers with low English proficiency, allowing them to perform at higher levels without waiting years to master a new language.
    * **Wage Growth:** By making roles like call center work more efficient, AI creates the potential for "wage boosts" tied to increased individual output.
* **Product Design Shift:** Governor Barr envisions a "reverse-engineered" financial sector where institutions design products specifically for LMI needs first, then adapt them for wealthier clients.
* **Curiosity as a Career Skill:** Barr identifies curiosity as the most vital skill for the AI era, enabling individuals to adapt to rapidly changing job requirements and technological tools.

## Critical Guardrails and Systemic Risks
* **Reinforcing Bias:** There is a significant risk that AI models could institutionalize and accelerate existing societal biases, particularly in credit decisioning and lending.
* **Financial Stability:** Advanced AI in trading could create new systemic vulnerabilities, including:
    * **Herd Behavior:** Accelerated market runs if multiple models react to the same stimuli simultaneously.
    * **Algorithmic Collusion:** The potential for independent AI systems to inadvertently coordinate in ways that undermine market integrity.
* **Privacy and Values Alignment:** Barr stressed the difficulty of protecting privacy in an AI-driven world and the necessity of ensuring AI "values alignment"—meaning systems must act according to the specific values of both the individual user and society at large.

## Bridging the "Trust Gap" and Adoption Barriers
* **Usage Disparities:** Current data suggests that individuals with less education and lower income are using frontier generative AI models less frequently, risking a "compounding advantage" for those already at the top.
* **The "Non-Judgmental" Interface:** Research shared by Tim Flacke suggests that LMI users are more likely to trust AI if it provides a non-judgmental environment.
    * **User Competence:** Effective AI tools should leave users feeling more competent and confident in their own abilities, rather than just delivering a passive answer.
    * **Institutional Trust:** Consumer willingness to use AI is highly correlated with their existing trust in the institution providing the technology.
* **Overcoming Invisible Barriers:** Many LMI individuals feel they do not "belong" in the world of investing; AI can help demystify these systems and provide a sense of agency.

## Addressing the "Scarcity" of Time and Focus
* **Creating Financial "Slack":** Barr discussed his research on "No Slack," noting that LMI families often face a scarcity of money, time, and focus.
    * **The "Uber Budgeting Tool":** AI can act as an automated assistant, managing complex financial tasks (like bill paying or insurance monitoring) while the user focuses on their primary job.
    * **Horizon Opening:** AI allows users to "zoom out" from immediate crises to model long-term goals, such as calculating the exact steps needed over 20 years to afford a child’s down payment on a home.
* **Evolution of Financial Education:** The field is shifting from "financial literacy" (classroom learning) to "financial capability" (just-in-time, behavioral insights). AI accelerates this by providing tailored advice at the exact moment a consumer is making a decision.

## Notable Quotes

> "It is possible that generative AI can help overcome inequality in our society and help promote financial inclusion, but only if we decide to do that with intentionality and purpose." — **Governor Michael Barr**

> "When young people ask me about their careers... the first thing I say to them is the most important skill you have is a skill of having a sense of curiosity because that's something you can carry with you your whole life." — **Governor Michael Barr**

> "People want to be sure that their data is safe... but they also need to feel that they're not being judged. I'm personally bullish that generative AI has the conditions to create that feeling." — **Tim Flacke**

briefings.title: Former Intel CEO on What Went Wrong, What's Next + Lovable CEO on the Real Promise of Vibe Coding
briefings.tldr: Intel’s decline was driven by a shift from technical to financial leadership that prioritized shareholder returns over R&D, while the future of software is being redefined by "vibe coding" platforms like Lovable that allow non-technical users to build and host enterprise-grade applications in hours.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Intel’s decline was driven by a shift from technical to financial leadership that prioritized shareholder returns over R&D, while the future of software is being redefined by "vibe coding" platforms like Lovable that allow non-technical users to build and host enterprise-grade applications in hours.

## The Decline and Restructuring of Intel
* **Leadership Shift:** Gelsinger attributes Intel’s "off the rails" period to the transition from deeply technical leaders (like Andy Grove) to "bean counters" and finance-driven executives.
    * When business leaders run technology companies, they tend to promote other business leaders, creating a disconnect from the technical trends that drive billion-dollar investments.
* **Capital Allocation Failures:** In the five to six years before Gelsinger’s return, Intel gave $100 billion to shareholders through dividends and stock buybacks.
    * This capital was diverted away from critical infrastructure; Intel had not built a new factory in a decade and failed to invest in EUV (Extreme Ultraviolet) lithography machines.
* **Missed Opportunities:** Intel famously passed on making chips for the iPhone and was slow to recognize the shift from CPUs to computationally dense GPUs for workloads like AI and high-performance computing (HPC).
* **The Foundry Strategy:** Intel is now pivoting to a "Foundry" model to compete with TSMC, standardized via Process Design Kits (PDKs) to manufacture chips for third parties, a departure from their historically proprietary model.

## Geopolitical Fragility and the Silicon Supply Chain
* **Taiwan’s Energy Vulnerability:** Taiwan currently has less than three weeks of energy reserves.
    * **The Blockade Risk:** A Chinese blockade would result in a "brownout" within 21 days. Because a semiconductor fab takes 90 days to restart after losing power, the economic impact would be "greater than the Great Depression."
* **Onshoring Progress:** Through the CHIPS Act, the US has increased its share of leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing from 12% to approximately 18%. 
* **Resiliency Requirements:** Gelsinger emphasizes that the world needs more resilient supply chains, noting that China has blockaded the Taiwan Straits seven times in the last four years as "practice."

## AI Economics and the Quantum Horizon
* **The Energy Ceiling:** Energy capacity acts as a natural "upper bound" on the AI bubble. Data center buildouts are limited by a grid that grew at only 1% for a decade.
* **Efficiency Targets:** To prevent a bubble burst, AI must become 10,000x more efficient. Gelsinger aims to drop the cost and energy per token by five orders of magnitude.
* **Quantum Computing Timeline:** Gelsinger predicts "Quantum Supremacy" and meaningful results in chemistry, biology, and logistics before 2030.
    * He anticipates solving fundamental encryption issues by 2032 or 2033.

## The "Vibe Coding" Revolution: Lovable
* **Rapid Scale:** Lovable has reached $500 million in revenue in just 20 months, with 1 million new projects being built on the platform every week.
* **SaaS Displacement:** Companies are using Lovable to replace 10+ internal bespoke tools (Salesforce, HubSpot, etc.) with custom-built applications, saving upwards of $1 million annually in licensing fees.
* **Beyond Mockups:** The platform has transitioned from simple wireframing to full-stack deployment, including:
    * **Automated Security:** Background security scans and data leak prevention.
    * **Integrated Payments:** One-prompt setup for secure financial transactions.
    * **Hosting:** Managing the underlying infrastructure (AWS) so users focus entirely on "vibe" and functionality.
* **Cost Efficiency:** Calacanis noted that an internal "Intranet" project that would have cost $500,000 and months of development two years ago was built by a non-technical employee using Lovable in four hours for less than $2,000 in total costs.

## Notable Quotes
> "When you're making these hardcore technical decisions that affect billions of dollars, you don't do that through a spreadsheet. That's a lousy investment, unless the technology trends make it the right investment." — **Pat Gelsinger**

> "The economic impact of a brownout of Taiwan is greater than the Great Depression... you never need to fire a shot. You just need to say, 'Great, no energy for three weeks.'" — **Pat Gelsinger**

> "The engineering is less of the bottleneck. It's more the question of what is the right thing to build." — **Anton Osika**

> "Software is going to become 100% bespoke... you don't need to be an engineer to create software, but you stay to build the business." — **Anton Osika**

briefings.title: Governor Cook moderates the “Emerging Innovation, AI and Financial Inclusion” panel, July 14, 2026
briefings.tldr: AI is democratizing high-quality financial advice and expanding credit access for underserved communities by leveraging alternative data and behavioral science, provided that developers prioritize rigorous, iterative "evals" and augment rather than replace human judgment.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
AI is democratizing high-quality financial advice and expanding credit access for underserved communities by leveraging alternative data and behavioral science, provided that developers prioritize rigorous, iterative "evals" and augment rather than replace human judgment.

## Transforming Financial Access through AI Personalization
* **Democratizing Wealth Management:** Governor Lisa Cook noted that while personalized financial advice was historically reserved for the wealthy, AI can provide high-quality guidance to all income levels.
    * In a recent small business credit survey, nearly 50% of small firms reported using AI, with 71% reporting increased productivity.
* **The "AI Navigator" Success:** Sarah Willis Air (SaverLife) detailed the impact of their AI-powered tool on 800,000 members across 50 states.
    * **Increased Actionability:** Users receiving AI-generated recommendations were 10 times more likely to follow through (e.g., contacting a credit counselor).
    * **Financial Outcomes:** Active users saw a $200 median increase in savings over three months, helping many overcome the common "$400 emergency expense" barrier.
* **Serving "Edge Cases":** Sanjay Subramanian highlighted that traditional banking was built for customers who fit standard profiles. AI can now analyze "messy" alternative data—such as utility and phone bill payments—to provide products to those with irregular incomes.

## Behavioral Science and Product Design
* **The "Bike Shop" Approach:** Laura Blatner (MIT) emphasized that product failure is often due to poor design rather than technology. The Lab focuses on "augmenting" human counselors rather than replacing them.
    * **Trust as a Barrier:** Early AI intake bots often fail because users are hesitant to share intimate financial details with a machine before a human relationship is established.
    * **Augmenting Human Expertise:** MIT is building tools that identify successful techniques from top-performing human counselors to help others adopt better phrasing and empathy in real-time.
* **Redirection vs. Paternalism:** Sarah Willis Air discussed using AI to nudge users away from high-risk behaviors like sports betting or crypto speculation, redirecting them toward long-term goals like homeownership.
* **The Scarcity Problem:** AI must be designed to respect the limited "cognitive bandwidth" of low-income users, ensuring tools simplify rather than complicate decision-making.

## Evaluation Frameworks and "Evals"
* **The Necessity of "Evals":** Laura Blatner argued that standardized benchmarks are insufficient. Organizations must build "applied evals" to test specific reasoning capabilities.
    * **Metric-Driven Testing:** Examples include measuring how many questions an AI asks before reaching a conclusion (efficiency) and its ability to reason through conflicting goals (e.g., prioritizing emergency repairs over 401k contributions).
* **Smart Synthetic Data:** While synthetic data can speed up testing, the panel warned it must be purposefully constructed to be representative. 
    * Simply duplicating a single conversation 1,000 times creates "lazy" data; it must reflect the diverse realities of the target user base.
* **Iterative Deployment:** The panel recommended a "drug trial" model: starting with small, closely monitored user groups and slowly pulling back guardrails as confidence in the AI's reliability grows.

## Institutional Roles and Regulatory Oversight
* **Breaking Silos:** Governor Cook emphasized the Federal Reserve's role as a "convener," bringing together tech firms, banks, community colleges, and nonprofits to ensure equitable technology adoption.
* **Economic Viability:** Sanjay Subramanian noted that AI is lowering the "cost to serve." Previously, if a customer cost $100 to maintain but only generated $40, they were excluded; AI shifts this economic reality.
* **Regulatory Responsibility:** The panel agreed that while innovation is fast-moving, there is a clear role for policy to codify model risk management and ensure AI doesn't perpetuate lending biases.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "Without evals, your AI financial advisor is just expensive advice trained on Reddit." — **Laura Blatner**, Head of Impact at the Bike Shop, MIT

> "Historically, personalized financial advice and wealth management were available mainly to those who could afford them. AI can make high-quality financial guidance accessible to everyone regardless of income or wealth." — **Governor Lisa Cook**, Federal Reserve Board

> "It’s enhancing judgment, not replacing it. I don’t think we’ll do ourselves any favor by replacing human judgment and agency." — **Sarah Willis Air**, Executive Vice President, SaverLife

> "The old financial system was not built for the edge cases... Gen AI is built to understand the messy, the complicated, and piece together something unique about the context of someone’s life." — **Sanjay Subramanian**, Technology Alliance Lead, PWC

briefings.title: I'm 80 and I wasted 25 years of my life. Don't make my mistake. - Howard Marks
briefings.tldr: Legendary investor Howard Marks emphasizes that superior results come from "second-level thinking" and the courage to act despite fear, noting that true success is defined by the autonomy to live life on your own terms.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Legendary investor Howard Marks emphasizes that superior results come from "second-level thinking" and the courage to act despite fear, noting that true success is defined by the autonomy to live life on your own terms.

## AI and the Future of Investment Judgment
Howard Marks recently updated his stance on AI, moving from skepticism to a recognition of its unprecedented potential, specifically regarding its **autonomy**.

*   **Distinctive Capabilities:** Unlike previous technological shifts (railroad, internet) which were merely tools for speed, AI possesses autonomy—the ability to figure out *how* to do a job without being told.
*   **The "Defrocking" of Mediocrity:** AI will likely "unfrock" investors who lack true talent, much like indexation exposed active managers who couldn't outperform averages.
*   **The Human Edge:** Marks believes experienced investors remain essential for two reasons:
    *   **The "Hair on the Neck" Test:** The ability to sense "bad people" or "wrong" deals through undefinable intuition and judgment.
    *   **Lack of Historical Data:** AI relies on pattern recognition; humans are still required to navigate unprecedented events where no training data exists.

## Investing Through Crisis and Fear
Marks recounts raising $11 billion for a distressed debt fund in 2008, highlighting that the best opportunities often feel the most terrifying.

*   **Building the Ark:** The best time to raise money is *before* a flood. Oaktree raised their massive fund in 2007–2008 because they saw market discipline disappearing, not because they knew exactly when the crash would happen.
*   **Acting Without Conviction:** Marks admits that during the Lehman Brothers collapse, he was not 100% confident. He argues that acting without trepidation in a crisis suggests something is wrong with the investor.
*   **The Rationality of Trepidation:** If you wait until there is nothing to fear, the opportunity has already passed. Success requires moving forward despite uncertainty.
*   **Quantitative Safety:** In 2008, Oaktree invested $500M/week for 15 weeks based on the logic that even if the companies they bought ended up being worth only 25% of their purchase price, the debt would still break even.

## The Architecture of Successful Partnerships
Marks and his co-founder, Bruce Karsh, have worked together for 39 years without a single fight. Marks attributes this to two core pillars:

*   **Shared Values:** A partnership fails if one person is a "cowboy" and the other is a "chicken." Disparate ethics or risk tolerances create friction during market shifts.
*   **Complementary Skills:** Marks and Karsh avoid overlap; Marks handles the external communication and "memos," while Karsh manages the money and stays out of the spotlight.
*   **Mutual Respect:** Acknowledging that the partner is better at certain tasks removes the "financial maximizer" ego that often destroys professional relationships.

## Success and Intentionality
Despite his legendary status, Marks admits he spent his first 25 years in the industry "unintentionally," making haphazard decisions based on luck and convenience.

*   **The Only Real Success:** Quoting Christopher Morley, Marks defines success as "living your life your own way." 
*   **The Late Start to Intentionality:** Marks did not start Oaktree until he was 49. He encourages younger people to find work that plays to their strengths and avoids their weaknesses, rather than following societal or parental pressure.
*   **Parenting via Autonomy:** Marks advocates for letting children make choices early—even incorrect ones—to build their own decision-making muscles, rather than asserting parental superiority.

## Insights on Warren Buffett and Reading
Marks shares observations from his long-standing relationship with Warren Buffett, particularly regarding the late Charlie Munger.

*   **The Buffett-Munger Dynamic:** Munger’s greatest contribution was moving Buffett away from "cigar butt" investing (buying cheap, low-quality companies for a final "puff" of value) toward buying "great companies at fair prices."
*   **Intellectual Humility:** Marks stresses that the most dangerous phrase in investing is "I am 100% convinced."
*   **Recommended Reading:**
    *   ***A Short History of Financial Euphoria*** **by John Kenneth Galbraith:** Essential for understanding the psychology behind market cycles.
    *   ***Fooled by Randomness*** **by Nassim Nicholas Taleb:** A guide to understanding how much of "success" is actually attributable to luck.

> "If you wait until you have nothing to be afraid about, probably the opportunity has passed." — Howard Marks

> "There is only one success: to live your life your own way." — Howard Marks (quoting Christopher Morley)

> "It ain't what you don't know that gets you into trouble. It's what you know for certain that just ain't true." — Howard Marks (quoting Mark Twain)

briefings.title: President Trump Participates in a Pennsylvania Defense and Innovation Summit
briefings.tldr: President Trump announced nearly $10 billion in new defense industrial base investments in Pennsylvania—projected to reach $20 billion—aimed at creating over 4,000 jobs and revitalizing the "Arsenal of Freedom" through aggressive deregulation, merit-based recruitment, and private-sector innovation.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
President Trump announced nearly $10 billion in new defense industrial base investments in Pennsylvania—projected to reach $20 billion—aimed at creating over 4,000 jobs and revitalizing the "Arsenal of Freedom" through aggressive deregulation, merit-based recruitment, and private-sector innovation.

## Industrial and Defense Investment in Pennsylvania
* **Massive Capital Injection:** The administration is announcing nearly $10 billion in new investments for Pennsylvania's defense industrial base, with expectations for the total to rise to $20 billion.
    * **Job Creation:** These investments are projected to create over 4,000 high-paying manufacturing jobs across the commonwealth.
    * **The "Money Belt":** Trump signaled a shift for Pennsylvania from being known as the "Rust Belt" to the "Money Belt," driven by domestic manufacturing.
* **Shipbuilding Revitalization:** Major focus on the Philadelphia Shipyard to build national security multi-mission vessels.
    * **International Partnerships:** Collaborative efforts with South Korean firm Hanwha to implement efficient shipbuilding techniques, aiming to scale production from one ship per year to 20.
* **Infrastructure and Energy:**
    * **Blackstone Commitment:** President and COO Jon Gray confirmed Blackstone is on track to invest $40 billion in digital and energy infrastructure over five years (50% higher than previous projections).
    * **Energy Strategy:** Focus on oil, gas, nuclear, and "clean beautiful coal," while explicitly rejecting wind energy as "intermittent" and "too expensive."

## Defense Innovation and "Department of War" Reform
* **Institutional Rebranding:** Trump and Secretary Pete Hegseth frequently referred to the "Department of War" (formerly Defense), emphasizing a shift from political correctness back to "winning wars."
    * **Bureaucratic "War of Attrition":** Secretary Hegseth highlighted efforts to dismantle Pentagon red tape that previously kept innovators out of the defense sector.
* **Key Technology Priorities:**
    * **The "Golden Dome":** Rapid development of a state-of-the-art missile defense shield for the U.S.
    * **Emergent Tech:** Massive investments in AI, robotics, autonomous vehicles, and space technology, specifically in the Pittsburgh area.
    * **Critical Components:** Trump urged business leaders to invest specifically in domestic **magnet manufacturing**, noting it as a current gap in the supply chain.
* **Procurement Efficiency:**
    * **Salesmanship:** Trump highlighted his role as a "salesman" for American military hardware (e.g., Boeing planes).
    * **Speed of Business:** Demand for contractors like General Dynamics and Lockheed Martin to build "faster" to meet modern threats.

## National Security and Domestic Policy
* **Merit-Based Military:** Trump emphasized that recruitment and advancement in the military and education are now strictly based on a "merit system," following recent Supreme Court decisions.
    * **Recruitment Surge:** Claims that the military is currently seeing "overflow crowds" and setting recruitment records due to a restored sense of national pride.
* **Trucking and Veteran Integration:**
    * **Illegal Alien Driver Ban:** The administration plans to remove illegal aliens from commercial trucking roles.
    * **Veteran Fast-Track:** Veterans who drove heavy trucks in the military will be automatically eligible for commercial driver's licenses (CDLs) to fill these roles.
* **Public Safety Successes:**
    * **Crime Reduction:** Claims of a 92% crime drop in Washington D.C. and successful "law and order" interventions during Mardi Gras in New Orleans using the National Guard.

## Corporate and Labor Partnerships
* **Lockheed Martin:** CEO Jim Taiclet announced the doubling of the Archbald, PA plant size, a $60 million investment adding 700 new jobs.
* **General Dynamics:** President Danny Deep highlighted a $2.5 billion investment in Rhoads Industries to support Navy submarine production, increasing that workforce five-fold.
* **Banking and Finance:** JP Morgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon stressed that a preeminent military is impossible without a preeminent economy, praising the "reignition" of the American dream through high-paying trade apprenticeships (e.g., welders starting at $80,000/year).
* **Labor Support:** Sean McGarvey (President of Building Trades Unions) committed a workforce of 300,000 current apprentices and 1,600 training centers to meet the construction needs of the defense buildup.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "To be a strong nation, you must be a manufacturing nation... Pennsylvania workers will build the ships, submarines, trucks, weapons, and industries that will ensure America remains the strongest and most powerful nation in the history of the world." — **President Donald Trump**

> "Our bureaucracy was built to keep most of you out. And we've been waging a war of attrition against the Pentagon bureaucracy to open up the aperture and make sure competition and speed and innovation and commercial options have a seat at the table." — **Secretary of War Pete Hegseth**

> "There is nothing more important for our country... than America maintain the preeminent military supported directly by the preeminent economy of the world. It’s none too soon... God knows this is now you guys have ignited the American dream." — **Jamie Dimon, CEO of JP Morgan Chase**

> "What’s happening here at this summit is really all the people we need in the room: the prime contractors, the energy leaders, the emergent technologies, the leaders in labor, the leaders in finance... to implement your vision of peace through strength." — **Senator David McCormick**

briefings.title: President Trump participates in Pennsylvania Defense and Innovation Summit — 7/15/2026
briefings.tldr: President Trump announced nearly $10 billion in new defense industrial investments for Pennsylvania, aiming to create 4,000 jobs and solidify the state as the "Arsenal of Freedom" through a manufacturing-first economic strategy and a $1.5 trillion national military budget.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
President Trump announced nearly $10 billion in new defense industrial investments for Pennsylvania, aiming to create 4,000 jobs and solidify the state as the "Arsenal of Freedom" through a manufacturing-first economic strategy and a $1.5 trillion national military budget.

## Major Defense and Industrial Announcements
* **Pennsylvania Investment:** A commitment of nearly $10 billion in new defense industrial base investments across the Commonwealth.
    * **Job Creation:** The projects are expected to generate over 4,000 high-paying manufacturing jobs.
    * **Shipbuilding:** Philadelphia Shipyard will build two national security multi-mission vessels worth $1.5 billion; Hanwha and Road Industries are partnering to bring next-generation shipbuilding back to the U.S.
    * **Submarines & Munitions:** General Dynamics will invest $2.5 billion in Roads Industries to accelerate Navy submarine production; artillery production in Scranton has expanded 4x.
* **National Security Infrastructure:**
    * **The "Golden Dome":** Significant investment in energy storage and autonomous technology to support a national missile defense shield.
    * **Strategic Readiness:** A proposed $1.5 trillion military budget for the upcoming year, focusing on "Made in the USA" equipment.

## Economic Strategy and Manufacturing Rebirth
* **Tariffs and Onshoring:** The administration is utilizing aggressive tariffs (up to 200% in some sectors) to force manufacturing back to the U.S., specifically targeting the semiconductor (chips) and automotive industries.
    * **Chip Production:** The President predicted the U.S. will produce 50% of the world’s chips by the end of his term without the direct subsidies used in previous administrations.
* **Tax and Financial Incentives:**
    * **Direct Relief:** Reiteration of "No Tax on Tips," "No Tax on Overtime," and "No Tax on Social Security."
    * **Industrial Incentives:** 100% expensing for capital investments (writing off plants and equipment in one year) and tax-deductible interest for American-made automobiles.
* **Energy Policy:**
    * **Energy Dominance:** Emphasis on "clean, beautiful coal," nuclear, and oil/gas, while explicitly rejecting wind energy as intermittent and environmentally damaging.
    * **Independent Power:** Encouraging AI and defense firms to build their own dedicated power plants to bypass the "fragile" national grid.

## Military and Workforce Reform
* **The "Department of War":** Secretary Pete Hegseth highlighted a shift from "Defense" back to "War," focusing on a culture of winning and eliminating bureaucratic "red tape" that historically blocked private-sector innovation.
* **Merit-Based Systems:** Following a Supreme Court ruling, the military and higher education have returned to a strict merit-based system for recruitment and admissions, which the President credits for record-breaking recruitment numbers.
* **Veteran Integration:** A new initiative will replace illegal alien commercial truck drivers with American veterans, granting automatic commercial licenses to those who drove heavy vehicles in the military.

## Innovation and Emerging Technology
* **Regional Hubs:** Transforming Pittsburgh into an international robotics and space technology hub through multi-hundred-million-dollar investments from firms like Voyager Technologies and Carnegie Robotics.
* **Technological Speed:** Secretary Hegseth and various CEOs (Lockheed Martin, General Dynamics) emphasized "moving at the speed of business," requiring primes to add manufacturing lines rather than just extra shifts.
* **Private Capital:** Blackstone announced it is on track to invest $40 billion in digital and energy infrastructure over five years—doubling previous commitments—to ensure the U.S. leads the AI race.

## Notable Quotes
> "To be a strong nation, you must be a manufacturing nation and have manufacturing jobs... Pennsylvania will play a key role in building the arsenal of freedom to defend our nation." — **President Donald J. Trump**

> "Our bureaucracy was built to keep most of you out... we’ve been waging a war of attrition against the Pentagon bureaucracy to open up the aperture and make sure competition and speed and innovation... have a seat at the table." — **Secretary of War Pete Hegseth**

> "There's nothing more important for our country... than America maintain the preeminent military supported directly by the preeminent economy of the world." — **Jamie Dimon, CEO of JPMorgan Chase**

> "Ships win battles. Shipyards win wars. And we are going to recreate what has been great in Philadelphia... to make American shipbuilding great again." — **Michael Coulter, President of Hanwha Defense USA**

briefings.title: The Future of AI: With Sir Demis Hassabis & Dame Wendy Hall

people.name: Wendy Hall
people.role: Regius Professor of Computer Science, University of Southampton

people.name: Gus Machado
people.role: Master, Worshipful Company of Information Technologists

briefings.tldr: Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) is likely achievable by 2030, necessitating an immediate "inverted" approach to education and the creation of an independent international governance body to mitigate existential risks while leveraging AI to solve "root node" scientific challenges like disease and climate change.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) is likely achievable by 2030, necessitating an immediate "inverted" approach to education and the creation of an independent international governance body to mitigate existential risks while leveraging AI to solve "root node" scientific challenges like disease and climate change.

## The Future of Education and AI Literacy
* **Inverting the Classroom:** Sir Demis Hassabis proposed a radical shift in secondary and primary education.
    * **Personalized Rote Learning:** AI tutors should handle repetitive learning at the student's individual pace outside the classroom.
    * **Human-Centric Schooling:** In-person time should focus on "human" skills: project management, entrepreneurialism, creativity, and judgment.
* **UK Skills Gap:** Dame Wendy Hall warned that while the UK was a first-mover in AI strategy (2017), it has since lost momentum. 
    * **International Competition:** Singapore and the UAE have overtaken the UK in strategy execution and adoption.
    * **Fragmented Oversight:** The UK currently lacks an AI skills champion or an independent body to oversee government AI units.
* **University Adaptations:** The University of Southampton is implementing an "AI Driving License" for all incoming students and integrating AI modules into every degree discipline, from history to physics.

## AGI Timelines and Global Governance
* **The 2030 Prediction:** Hassabis defines AGI as a system exhibiting all human cognitive capabilities and expects it to arrive within 5–10 years (roughly 2030).
* **International AI Agency:** Both speakers advocated for a new, independent international body for AI standards and safety, potentially spinning out of the UN but remaining autonomous.
    * **Urgency:** Even if the timeline is 10 years, current institutions are not fit for purpose to handle the "agentic era" where software makes autonomous decisions.
* **Key Risks:**
    * **Biorisk and Cyber:** The misuse of general-purpose technologies by rogue actors for harmful biological or digital ends.
    * **The "Tragedy of the Commons":** While lab leaders generally want guardrails, market competition incentivizes companies to "defect" from safety protocols for profit.
    * **Deepfakes:** A "no-brainer" requirement for invisible watermarking and detection systems is needed to protect information integrity.

## UK Economic Strategy and Infrastructure
* **Energy as Intelligence:** Hassabis argued that in the new industrial base, "watts translate to tokens." 
    * **High Costs:** The UK’s high energy costs are a direct threat to its AI industry competitiveness.
    * **The Data Center Flip:** Hall suggested that in the future, towns will want data centers locally because they will eventually become generators/recyclers of heat and power for the community.
* **The Scaling Problem:** The UK is world-class at research and "unicorns" but fails at the "growth stage."
    * **Stock Exchange Issues:** Significant reforms are needed to the London Stock Exchange to prevent high-growth tech companies (like ARM) from listing in the US.
* **The "DeepMind Effect":** 74% of UK VC dollars in Q1 2024 went to AI. Notably, 10% of that funding went to companies founded by DeepMind alumni, proving the value of "anchor" companies in local ecosystems.

## AI as the Ultimate Tool for Science
* **"Root Node" Problems:** Hassabis chose protein folding (AlphaFold) because solving it opened thousands of other doors in biology. 
    * **Massive Adoption:** Over 3 million researchers globally have used AlphaFold.
* **Beyond Biology:** DeepMind is applying similar AI logic to:
    * **Weather Prediction:** Best-in-class hurricane path prediction (used by the US Met Office).
    * **Material Science:** Discovering new materials for batteries and solar cells.
    * **Fusion Energy:** Using AI to contain plasma in fusion reactors.
* **Isomorphic Labs:** A UK-based spin-out reimagining drug discovery as an "information processing" challenge rather than a trial-and-error process.

## Ethical Imperatives and Social Cohesion
* **The Diversity Crisis:** Dame Wendy Hall emphasized that AI leadership remains a "monoculture."
    * **Safety through Diversity:** AI is "too important to be left to men" or any single demographic; diverse perspectives are required to prevent the hard-coding of bias into AGI.
* **Public Resistance:** There is a growing "AI-free" movement among students and the public who feel powerless against big tech. 
* **Teamwork, Not Replacement:** Both speakers view the future as "human-AI teams," where AI handles "grunge work" and humans focus on high-level creativity and complex interpersonal roles like medicine.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "I would suggest something much more radical... we need to invert the classroom. School should be about people skills, projects, and judgment... rote learning should be aided by personalized AI." — **Sir Demis Hassabis**

> "You cannot be world champions at regulation only. You’ve got to also be leading in the technology to have a seat at the table." — **Sir Demis Hassabis**

> "Computing is too important to be left to men... we have to think about what type of society we're building before we reach the holy grail of AGI." — **Dame Wendy Hall**

> "I wouldn’t swap my Nobel for any amount of money. I always cared about the research and what it could do for humanity." — **Sir Demis Hassabis**

briefings.title: Warren Buffett: I initiated Berkshire Hathaway's investment in Alphabet
briefings.tldr: Warren Buffett revealed he initiated Berkshire Hathaway's multi-billion-dollar stake in Alphabet, which now exceeds $31 billion including a recent $10 billion private placement.
briefings.summary_markdown:
### TL;DR
Warren Buffett revealed he initiated Berkshire Hathaway's multi-billion-dollar stake in Alphabet, which now exceeds $31 billion including a recent $10 billion private placement. While acknowledging that tech giants are now playing a massive capital-spending game on AI, Buffett defended the investment based on Alphabet's fundamental earnings power and returns on capital.

## Alphabet Investment & Portfolio Scale
* **Alphabet Position Size:** Berkshire Hathaway holds a stake in Alphabet exceeding **$31 billion**.
  * The position began building in the **third quarter of 2025** and accelerated after **Greg Abel** took over as CEO of Berkshire.
  * A **$10 billion private stock purchase** of Alphabet shares was added just last month.
* **Portfolio Ranking:** Alphabet ranks as roughly the **number 5 or 6** holding in Berkshire's portfolio (or **number 3** if fully counting marketable securities and the $10 billion private placement).
  * It sits behind Apple and American Express among equity holdings, though fully-owned subsidiaries like Burlington Northern Railroad carry higher standalone values.
  * It ranks ahead of Bank of America and Coca-Cola (which Buffett noted has been owned for **45 years**).

## Philosophy on "Good Businesses" & Capital Returns
* **Definition of a Good Business:** Buffett defines a superior business as one that consistently earns high returns on capital over an extended period, significantly outperforming riskless government treasuries yielding **$20, 30, or $40 billion a year**.
* **American Express Benchmark:** While typical banks earn **13% to 14%** on capital, American Express earns **30% plus** on capital without incurring higher relative risk.
* **The Charlie Munger Principle:** Longtime partner Charlie Munger insisted that businesses must generate real cash rather than just engage in "sexy things," possessing the ability to either distribute that cash or profitably reemploy it.
* **Flaws of Wall Street:** Buffett criticized Wall Street analysts for focusing on short-term quarterly results and selling hype rather than analyzing internal rates of return.

## Tech Stocks, CAPEX, & The AI Game
* **Shift on Technology:** Despite historically avoiding tech stocks and labeling himself as someone who doesn't understand them, Buffett defended the Alphabet stake, noting he also previously built Berkshire's massive Apple position (which he categorized as a consumer company).
* **Massive Capital Expenditures:** Unlike the asset-light software era that Buffett previously avoided, today's tech giants and hyperscalers (including Alphabet, Amazon, and Microsoft) are deploying hundreds of billions in heavy CAPEX for AI.
  * Buffett compared this to old industrial spending, noting that companies like the railroad or IBM faced industry-shifting disruptions when competitors arrived to better serve customers.
* **Customer Satisfaction vs. Market Hype:** Buffett emphasized that satisfying customers is paramount over time, contrasting the pragmatic approach of a grocery store owner (like his experience in his grandfather's grocery store operating since **1869**) with the speculative dreams of Wall Street.

## Historical Perspective on Investing
* **Historical Precedents:** Buffett pointed to John D. Rockefeller as potentially the most successful long-term investor, compounding wealth steadily through the oil and gas industry over **150 to 200 years**.
* **Early Tech Venture:** Buffett recalled his early association with technology in **1958**, when he and friends started a company called **Data Documents** after reading that IBM had settled an antitrust suit by divesting 50% of its best business capacity.

## Notable Quotes
> "I initiated. I mean, I normally wouldn't give you an answer on something like that, but I will... We talk all the time. Every day. I mean, and but he is the decider."  
> — *Warren Buffett* (on who decided to purchase Alphabet)

> "The important thing is to buy a good business and to buy it on the right terms, and then get the right person to run it."  
> — *Warren Buffett*

> "Wall Street can be very dumb... in terms of they can dream, but a guy with a grocery store can't dream."  
> — *Warren Buffett*
